newsitem.title: USA: North Dakota unemployment falls to 2.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: North Dakota unemployment falls to 2.9 pct.

text.p: North Dakota's unemployment rate dropped from 3.2 percent in March to 2.9 percent in April, the lowest mark since the state began keeping records in 1958, the state's job service department has reported.
The seasonally adjusted unemployment rate remained unchanged at 2.8 percent in April, the department said in a statement released Thursday.
Information used for the projections was collected before the Red River Valley flooding, the department noted.
Non-agricultural wage and salary employment rose 2.1 percent in April to 311,800 compared to the year before, including gains in seven industries, the department reported.

Finance, insurance and real estate posted a 6.4 percent gain over April 1996; manufacturing, 4.9 percent; services, 4.3 percent; wholesale trade, 1.4 percent; mining, 1.3 percent; retail trade, 0.7 percent; and transportation, communication and utilities, 0.5 percent.
